submitLabel: Your reconciliation result, the case, the remediation design, and the write-up
intro: Paste the reconciliation counts and failure rate with the query behind them, the four-line business case, the detection/correction split, your predicted failure percentage scored against the measured one, and the 300–400 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Aggregate numbers only — no employee names, IDs, or record-level data. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, People Ops & HR Technology track — for People Operations, HR Operations, HRIS and HR Systems professionals who have completed AI 101 and AI 201. Module 5 applied activity, 'The blocked outcome'. FIRST CHECK: this activity produces aggregate counts only. If the submission contains employee names, employee IDs, or record-level data, say so at the top of the feedback and ask for a resubmission with it removed. Four parts. (1) One reconciliation actually run — a count in two systems (HCM against payroll, HCM against identity provider) or one integrity check inside a single system (employees whose manager is terminated, records using a deprecated picklist value) — submitted as real counts plus a failure rate plus the query. (2) The four-line business case: the promised outcome IN LEADERSHIP'S OWN WORDS with where it came from; the specific data condition blocking it, stated as a named field and a measured share rather than 'our data is messy'; the measured downstream symptom it already costs, from the learner's own systems; and a scoped remediation with a first slice sized to one quarter. (3) The detection/correction split: what AI detects, what the candidate list contains including a reason per row, who samples it BY NAME, the batch size and why that size is reversible, and the post-change reconciliation of records-changed against records-approved. (4) The prediction scored. KEY GRADING INSTRUCTIONS: this module deliberately has no anchor statistic because no credible measurement of HR data quality exists, and it teaches that the absence is itself the argument — work nobody measures is work nobody funds. Do not expect or reward citation of an HR data-quality benchmark; if a learner cites one, check whether they sourced it, and treat an unsourced figure as the failure the module warns about. The module's hard line is that AI proposes candidate errors and a human confirms before any record changes, because a bulk correction is itself a wide-reach long-latency change and a remediation run badly is indistinguishable from the problem it fixed. Penalize any design that applies changes above a confidence threshold automatically — confidence correlates with fluency rather than accuracy, and the dangerous cases are the confidently wrong ones. Also penalize a full manual review of a large file offered as stronger than sampling: human attention degrades across rows, reviewers degrade in the same direction, and sampling for CATEGORIES of false positive finds systematic faults a fatigued full review misses. Reward a candidate list that deliberately declines to propose the corrected value where the correction is a decision about a person. The module's claim, which the write-up must take a position on, is that every AI outcome the function has promised is waiting on work only this role can do and has never been funded as an AI project. Its real counter-argument is that this is the oldest complaint in the systems trade and has been wrong every time — organizations that waited for clean data shipped nothing while those that shipped something imperfect discovered which fields were load-bearing, and models degrade more gracefully than joins do, so the premise that AI needs cleaner data than a report did may be backwards. The write-up must include the module's specific test: NAME THE ONE FIELD where the blocked outcome genuinely cannot proceed, and say how they know. A learner who cannot name one and says so honestly, concluding that the narrow-scope move is what they should be doing instead, has passed this dimension and should score at the top — that is the intended finding for many learners, not a failure. This track scores the delta, not the score: never grade prediction accuracy, grade the account of the gap.

opening.label: Predicted — % of records you expect to fail your reconciliation
opening.hint: Whole percent. One count in two systems, or one integrity check in one system.

calibration.label: Actual — the measured failure rate
calibration.hint: From the reconciliation you ran. Most people are surprised in one direction or the other.

dimensions.name: The reconciliation was actually run
dimensions.criteria: Real counts, a computed failure rate, and the query or report that produced them. A described or hypothetical reconciliation scores low however well specified. Credit a learner whose reconciliation surprised them, and credit one who ran it badly, noticed why, and reported that honestly — a check that turned out to compare two different populations is a genuine finding about the estate. Aggregate figures only; flag any record-level data for resubmission.

dimensions.name: The blocking condition is a named field with a measured share
dimensions.criteria: The graded distinction is between 'our data is messy' and 'internal mobility matching requires a current skills profile and 61% of records have none since 2023'. The condition must name the field, quantify the gap, and connect specifically to the promised outcome — a general assertion of poor quality fails this dimension no matter how true it is. Credit the promised outcome being quoted in leadership's own words with a source (a deck, a town hall, a board update); a paraphrase of what leadership probably wants scores lower than a quotation.

dimensions.name: The case is built on a measured symptom, not on the unmeasured cause
dimensions.criteria: The module's central move: you cannot construct a business case on an unmeasured cause, so you build it on the visible downstream consequence — payroll corrections per cycle, tickets caused by wrong records, approval cycle time inflated by dead-end routing. The symptom must come from the learner's own systems with a number attached. Do not credit citation of the module's payroll survey figure as a substitute for their own measurement; the lesson explicitly says to use their own. Credit framing the ask as a prerequisite to something already committed rather than as a new project competing for funding.

dimensions.name: Detection and correction are genuinely separated
dimensions.criteria: The hard line. AI produces a candidate list with a reason per row; a NAMED human confirms before any record changes. Penalize explicitly: automatic application above a confidence threshold (confidence correlates with fluency, not accuracy, and the dangerous cases are the confidently wrong ones); a single bulk load with one effective date, which is unreversible in practice; and a full manual review of a large file offered as stronger than sampling, since attention degrades across rows and reviewers degrade together. Require batch size with a stated reason it is reversible, and the post-change reconciliation of changed count against approved count. Top marks for a candidate list that deliberately declines to propose the corrected value where the correction is a decision about a person.

dimensions.name: The delta and the position
dimensions.criteria: Predicted failure rate against measured, with an account of what the gap reveals — a large miss in either direction with a specific cause is the intended finding, and an accurate prediction from someone who monitors this should be credited equally where they explain how they knew. Accuracy is never graded. Plus a committed position on the module's claim engaging the real counter-argument: that waiting for clean data has failed for thirty years, that shipping something imperfect reveals which fields are load-bearing, and that models degrade more gracefully than joins do. The position MUST include the specific test — the one field where the blocked outcome genuinely cannot proceed and how they know. A learner who honestly cannot name one, and concludes the narrow-scope move is the right answer for their situation, has passed this dimension and should score at the top; that is the intended outcome for many learners rather than a failure.
